A.claim: Literature state for the residual family (4,4,p), p odd prime: (4,4,3) solved via (n,n,3); (4,4,5) solved via (2n,2n,5) [Bennett 2006]; for general p only the First Case (p does not divide xyz) is proved, for p != 7 (Dieulefait, arXiv:math/0304425, Q-curves and modular congruences). The Second Case is open.

B.claim: Kernel-checked first factorisation step for signature (p,p,r), p odd prime: A^p+B^p = (A+B)*S with S = sum A^i(-B)^{p-1-i}, S = p*A^{p-1} mod (A+B), and for coprime A,B every common divisor of A+B and S divides p; hence in a counterexample (A+B)*S = C^r with gcd | p.
